raw_response:
I will not start from empty talk. I will do what worked for me before, then move a little where I have to. On 15.3 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steady money here, and I have well water, so I can protect yield better on that land. Cotton costs more labor, especially topping, spraying, and picking, and at my age with some family working away, I will not spread cotton too wide. I will keep 3 mu of cotton and put 12.3 mu into wheat-maize.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed. Around here, if wheat is thin in winter or short of fertilizer at jointing, the yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I will put enough base fertilizer in, then chase nitrogen once more in spring, and I will water 3 times if the year is normal: once before winter if soil is dry, once at jointing, once at grain filling. I will spray 3 times if needed, mainly for weeds, aphids, and rust or scab pressure. On my wheat land, I will aim for about 500 kg per mu if weather does not turn bad.

For summer maize, I will do it the fast way after wheat harvest. I will not waste time with heavy tillage there. I will seed quickly, keep enough fertilizer under it, and use hybrid seed because the stand is more even and yield is safer. Maize can eat fertilizer, so I will not cut too hard there. I will water 2 times in a normal year, mainly around big flare and grain filling if rain is short. I will spray about 2 times, one for weeds and one for insects like armyworm or aphid if I see pressure. If the stand is good, I will look for about 650 kg per mu.

For cotton, I will keep only the better piece of ground for it. Cotton needs more watching than wheat or maize, so I will not plant too much. I will use hybrid cotton seed, give it enough potash, and spray more times than the grain crops because bugs on cotton do not wait for anybody. I will water about 3 times with the well if rain is short. I will still fertilize cotton well because if bolls set badly, I cannot make that back later. On cotton I will look for around 320 kg seed cotton per mu in a decent year.
